status: Lou's conversation, drafted by Claude from docs/INTERVIEW_DRAFT.md for Cory to review (E25). Asked after payment while the report is read. Plain code walks this list; typed answers are stored exactly as written and never sent to a model.

nodes.text: Did the inspector tell you anything out loud, in person or on the phone, about what they would or wouldn't check? Even a small comment helps.
nodes.why: Things said out loud can matter as much as what is written.

nodes.text: What did they tell you? Tap everything that fits.
nodes.why: Each answer helps us ask the right follow-up.
options: They told me what they would check
They told me what they would not check
They told me how long the visit would be
They told me about a cost or package limit
They told me some areas could not be reached
They told me their findings out loud

nodes.text: What did they say they would look at?
nodes.why: So we know what you were expecting.

when.includes: They told me what they would check

nodes.text: What did they say they wouldn't look at? Tell it the way you remember it.
nodes.why: So we know what was set aside, in your words.

when.includes: They told me what they would not check

nodes.text: How long did they say it would take, and about how long were they there?
nodes.why: Time on site shapes what could be checked.

when.includes: They told me how long the visit would be

nodes.text: What did they say the price or package included, and what was left out?
nodes.why: A package can explain why some steps were not taken.

when.includes: They told me about a cost or package limit

nodes.text: Which areas did they say they couldn't get to, and what was the reason they gave?
nodes.why: Places that could not be reached are unknown, not clear or affected.

when.includes: They told me some areas could not be reached

nodes.text: What did they tell you they saw or found? Even a rough memory helps.
nodes.why: It helps us compare what you heard with what the report says.

when.includes: They told me their findings out loud

nodes.text: Tell us what you remember.
nodes.why: So nothing you remember gets lost.

nodes.text: What made you get this inspection? Tap everything that fits.
nodes.why: Your reason helps us see what the report was meant to answer.
options: A concern about health or comfort

nodes.text: Tell us a little about why.
nodes.why: In your own words.

nodes.text: Is there an insurance claim open for this?
nodes.why: A claim can change what records matter.

nodes.text: About when did you first notice it?
nodes.why: Timing helps us read the report in context.

nodes.text: Is there a closing date or deadline coming up?
nodes.why: A deadline can explain why some steps were rushed or skipped.

nodes.text: Were you there for the visit?
nodes.why: Being there changes what you saw and heard.

nodes.text: About what date was the visit?
nodes.why: Dates help line up the report with what happened.

nodes.text: Was anyone else there, like an agent, a seller, or a contractor?
nodes.why: Others at the visit may have seen or said something too.

nodes.text: Who was there? First names or roles are fine.
nodes.why: So the record is complete.

nodes.text: Did the inspector show you anything during the visit, like a moisture reading or a photo?
nodes.why: What you were shown may not be in the report.

nodes.text: What did they show you?
nodes.why: So we can compare it with the report.

nodes.text: Did the inspector take any samples?
nodes.why: Samples lead to lab results that belong with the report.

nodes.text: Do you know which lab the samples went to, or when you got the results?
nodes.why: So we know where the lab results come from.

nodes.text: Did you see the inspector use any tools or instruments, like a moisture meter or a thermal camera?
nodes.why: Tools and readings are what a report's findings rest on.

nodes.text: Which ones do you remember?
nodes.why: So we can look for them in the report.

nodes.text: What were the conditions at the time of the visit? Tap everything that fits.
nodes.why: Weather and the home's condition can change what a visit finds.
options: The air conditioning or heat was off
The home was empty or unoccupied

nodes.text: Did the report match what the inspector told you at the visit?
nodes.why: A difference is worth a friendly question, and a match is good to know.

nodes.text: What was different?
nodes.why: So the question for the inspector can be specific.

nodes.text: Has this home had mold, water damage, or another inspection before?
nodes.why: Earlier events can explain what a report finds.

nodes.text: What do you know about it?
nodes.why: Even a rough idea helps.

nodes.text: Have you talked with the inspector since you got the report?
nodes.why: Later conversations may already answer a question.

nodes.text: What did they say?
nodes.why: So we don't ask you to ask something already answered.

nodes.text: Is there anything else you think we should know?
nodes.why: Last chance to add anything in your own words.
